claims.head: A shadow job for Mikheyev, Cirelli and Holmberg
claims.call: The Lightning’s L2 (Mikheyev, Cirelli and Holmberg) spends at least 54% of its 5-on-5 time against the Hurricanes’ first line, against about 37% with no line matching.
claims.body: At home, the Lightning keep sending Cirelli’s line (Mikheyev, Cirelli and Holmberg) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jon Cooper has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Hurricanes’ first line is Carrier, Aho and Svechnikov.

TBL.head: Close, but the Hurricanes have the slight edge
TBL.body: Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately, while Tampa Bay may be without Hagel. Then again, Tampa Bay gets Hagel back and has home-ice advantage, and Carolina will be without Ehlers. The Lightning can tip it if they get good looks.

CAR.head: The Hurricanes start a half-step ahead
CAR.body: Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately, while Tampa Bay may be without Hagel. Then again, Carolina will be without Ehlers, and Tampa Bay gets Hagel back and has home-ice advantage. Still, it’s close: the Lightning can make it interesting if they get good looks.

story.head: Clash of the titans
paras: The Lightning (15-6-2) lost 6-2 to Buffalo on Sunday, while the Hurricanes have won two in a row. Two of the league’s best teams meet. Going in, the Hurricanes are first in the Metropolitan (second in the NHL) and the Bolts second in the Atlantic (tied for sixth).

The Hurricanes take away shots from the point (lowest) and create more chances on the penalty kill than anyone (1st). They also give up a lot of dangerous shots (32nd), so the Lightning could find some good looks against them. Carolina has scored 4.17 goals a game, the most in the league, and allowed 2.25, the second fewest. The Lightning ice the puck less than almost anyone (3rd), but don’t block many shots (29th). They also keep shots away better than almost anyone (3rd), and something has to give when the Hurricanes’ shooting runs into their defense.

Sebastian Aho (13 G / 20 A / 33 P in 24 GP) leads the Hurricanes in scoring and is tied for seventh in the NHL, with seven points in his last five games. Logan Stankoven (11 G / 13 A / 24 P in 24 GP) is next in line. Nikita Kucherov (10 G / 22 A / 32 P in 23 GP) leads the Lightning in scoring and is tied for ninth in the NHL, with six goals in eight games against Carolina since 2023-24. Jake Guentzel (13 G / 15 A / 28 P in 23 GP) has a team-high 13 goals.
Brandon Bussi (5-2-2 / .879 SV% in 9 GS) is expected to start for Carolina, and Andrei Vasilevskiy (11-5-1 / .895 SV% in 17 GS) for Tampa Bay.
At home, Jon Cooper likes to send Mikheyev, Cirelli and Holmberg out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Carrier, Aho and Svechnikov.
